ceilings: escalation data per region/area beside #93's seats: a full-law region seats the whole ladder; a frontier town may cap at sought; a place with no law presence caps at reported (known, and that is all — #270 still costs in full). A ceiling is the place's authored truth, not a difficulty dial (#70). The depths seat no responders — data, with no consequence drawn here
decay: unwitnessed clean days decay the ACTIVE rung one step at a time, never below reported while facts stand unresolved; the clock is #275's clean-conduct clock. Decay cools pursuit, never forgives: resolution is #275 (surrender/restitution/service) or #230 (findings). A fresh witness fact re-raises a quiet incident at any time — the ledger does not forget

ladder.baseRung: data per deed class, tempered by #269 ledger history (#271's wanted-tempering seat is this machinery)
ladder.rule: rungs never drop for leaving the area — leaving moves the search, not the rung

rungs.name: reported
rungs.what: a report exists; local people know. No pursuit — the cost is #270's tallies and a waiting record

rungs.name: sought
rungs.what: the place's own responders (#93 seats) challenge on sight — a #210-class meeting on the law's terms: answer, yield, or run, each writing its own facts

rungs.name: pursued
rungs.what: active search from the LAST-SEEN place (#7 area + beat of the last witness/report) outward through #297 terrain on #93-class movement — a geography that can be learned, outrun honestly, or waited out

rungs.name: hunt
rungs.what: the region answers with its best (authored Rangers of #37/#100 class); the report is heard beyond its home group (#270 neighbours). Reserved for the gravest witnessed deed classes, as data

note: #272's flow and #275's clock are cited by commissioned subject (List 28 mid-build); reconciliation owed at List 28's landing, per STAGING.
yielding: a designed verb at any rung: ends the active incident on the spot (the search stands down), routes facts to #230 findings / #275 roads. Quoted in so it cannot drift: discipline never confiscates a Mochi (#230) — and neither does surrender; a stolen Mochi's return is restitution, #273/#275's transaction
